transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-03-20 15:00 UTC
Duration: 62 minutes
Attendees: Avery Chen (Redwood AE), Samir Rao (Redwood SE), Maya Ortiz (Redwood CSM); Lena Ortiz (Stonehaven CTO), Marcus Doyle (Platform Eng), Priya Sharma (Security), Tom Vasquez (DevOps), Rachel Kim (PM)

Summary: quick kickoff for implementation and ops handoff. Discussed network connectivity (VPC peering), security requirements (KMS/SOC2), pilot scope (3 endpoints: chat, embeddings, rerank), telemetry needs, and an initial performance baseline. Lots of Q&A about dedicated vs hosted, data residency, and fallback behaviors. Agreed next steps and owners.

[00:00] Avery Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, we can see a full table, hi hi, I'm Avery from Redwood, im the AE on the account.
[00:12] Lena Ortiz: Hi Avery, hi Samir, thanks, excited to get started. A little bit of background, we want to ship semantic search and a chat assistant inside our operator dashboard. Security is a big blocker for us.
[00:25] Samir Rao: Great, Samir here from the SE side. I'll be driving the technical integration and run the baseline. Quick ask — can each of you just state what success looks like for this pilot?
[00:38] Rachel Kim: For product, success is fast relevance — embeddings that raise click-through by 15% and chat responses under 500ms median.
[00:50] Marcus Doyle: From platform, success is a stable endpoint with predictable throughput, preferably dedicated-ish capacity or reserved so we don't see noisy neighbor spikes.
[01:02] Priya Sharma: From security, SOC 2 evidence, KMS integration, and audit logs for any PII flows. We also need to understand data retention.
[01:12] Avery Chen: Perfect. On the control plane we offer Hosted API, Dedicated pools, and Private VPC options. For pilot most customers start hosted to iterate faster then move to Dedicated or Private depending on security. We can map that to your SLOs.
[01:30] Tom Vasquez: Can you walk through what VPC peering looks like? We're on AWS, need to know firewall rules and CIDR.
[01:40] Samir Rao: Sure — for Private we do a customer-managed VPC peering approach. You'll open TLS egress from internal subnets to Redwood ingress CIDR; we'll send a short diagram. For hosted we just use TLS to our public endpoints but you can restrict via IP allowlist. Note: firewalls sometimes block large streaming payloads so we'll call that out.
[02:05] Rachel Kim: Is there a difference in latency between hosted and dedicated?
[02:10] Samir Rao: Typically dedicated on a pinned pool gives you lower P50 and more predictable P90s. Hosted varies by capacity; we do smart routing and fallbacks but the tail can be higher during spikes. For numbers, I can run a baseline.
[02:25] Marcus Doyle: We have a 500ms median SLO — is that realistic for chat at 2k token context?
[02:34] Samir Rao: 2k tokens is plausible under 500ms median with the right model variant and batching. If you hit 8k tokens median will rise; also depends on model architecture. We'll propose a quantization and batching profile.
[02:50] Priya Sharma: About encryption — we need customer-managed KMS for keys at rest. Is that supported?
[02:56] Avery Chen: Yes, Private deployments support customer KMS/HSM. For hosted we offer envelope encryption and can integrate with BYOK in Dedicated/Private. We'll include KMS notes in the security packet.
[03:10] Lena Ortiz: Any notable gotchas for KV cache or sessions? We run a lot of retrieval-heavy prompts with short prefixes.
[03:20] Samir Rao: KV cache is important; we do continuous batching and automatic prefix caching. One thing to watch for is tokenization differences between your preprocessor and model which can affect cache hit rates — we sometimes see "KV cash" in transcripts, but I mean cache — ha. We'll send a short doc on aligning tokenizers.
[03:40] Tom Vasquez: On networking, we also need to know what ports and egress CIDR to open for healthchecks and telemetry.
[03:50] Maya Ortiz (CSM): We'll include a one-page connectivity checklist in the packet.
[03:55] [audio glitch] Speaker 3: (unintelligible)
[04:05] Avery Chen: Ok planner, pilot scope: three endpoints — chat assistant, embeddings for search, and reranking API. Pilot will use hosted for accelerated dev; if security gating appears we'll move to Dedicated. Timeline proposed: 2-week integration, 2-week pilot, then evaluation. Does that align?
[04:25] Rachel Kim: That works for product. We'll aim to provide sample payloads and queries by Friday.
[04:33] Marcus Doyle: We will need a staging environment with VPC peering for load tests before go-live.
[04:40] Samir Rao: Understood. I'll set expectations for load tests: we recommend a synthetic workload that mirrors your bursts and a steady-state. For cost planning, batching and KV cache reduce tokens costs significantly.
[05:00] Priya Sharma: Audit logs — how granular are they? We need per-request traces and token-level cost attributions for our internal chargeback.
[05:10] Avery Chen: Console exposes token-level cost breakdowns and per-route traces; audit logs can be forwarded to your SIEM. For the Private offering we can increase retention windows.
[05:24] Priya Sharma: Great, retention windows — we have to retain certain logs for 12 months for audits.
[05:30] Avery Chen: Noted. We'll flag retention options and any add-on costs.
[05:36] Marcus Doyle: On SSO — how long is SAML integration typically?
[05:40] Maya Ortiz: SAML SSO usually 1-2 weeks depending on your IdP and whether you want role mapping. We can do an initial admin invite quickly.
[05:50] Lena Ortiz: We need a dedicated trial contract for proof-of-concept — someone mentioned a short-term reserved capacity?
[05:58] Avery Chen: Yes we can do a small reserved capacity block for the pilot for predictable perf; pricing will depend on size and duration. I'll follow up with a pilot quote.
[06:10] Tom Vasquez: For the baseline run, what telemetry should we provide?
[06:15] Samir Rao: Sample payloads, concurrency targets, and typical request size distribution. If you can provide a day of real traffic (anonymized) that's ideal. We'll also ask for token distribution histograms.
[06:30] Rachel Kim: About model choices — do you recommend open models or Redwood-verified curated models?
[06:36] Samir Rao: We'll recommend a model family depending on quality vs cost. For embeddings, vector models we recommend X-family; for chat, we'll propose a mid-tier open model for pilot to control cost, upgrade if quality needs. We'll include recommended variants and quant profiles.
[06:55] Marcus Doyle: Any compliance red flags for non-prod data? Our staging sometimes has scrambled PII and we need to be sure it's handled correctly.
[07:02] Priya Sharma: Yes we avoid any production PII in staging but can provide redacted examples. Document what data is transient versus stored.
[07:12] Avery Chen: Agreed, we'll document data flows and indicate optional data-in-transit encryption details and retention.
[07:20] [15 minute jump, summarizing technical deep-dive]
[22:40] Samir Rao: Quick note on perf: I'll run a 2-step baseline — short context (2k tokens) and long context (8k tokens). Expect to see median delta of ~1.5–3x for longer contexts depending on model. I'll deliver a matrix with P50/P90 and cost estimates.
[22:58] Marcus Doyle: Please include burst capacity behavior — we want to avoid noisy neighbors for heavy inference spikes.
[23:06] Samir Rao: For Dedicated we can reserve headroom and configure autoscale policies. We'll also discuss fallback model variants to preserve latency under strain.
[23:20] Rachel Kim: Who will be our day-to-day contact?
[23:24] Avery Chen: Maya will be your CSM for adoption; I and Samir will be on technical as needed.
[23:33] Maya Ortiz: I'll run weekly syncs during onboarding and share playbooks.
[23:38] Lena Ortiz: Ok, let's recap next steps.
[23:42] Avery Chen: Recap: Avery will send security docs and pilot quote; Samir will run latency baseline and share batching/quant configs; Marcus will provide networking CIDRs and sample payloads; Priya will share compliance contacts. We'll schedule pilot kickoff for 2027-03-29 tentatively.
[23:58] Tom Vasquez: Small thing — is there an SDK recommended for Node vs Python?
[24:04] Samir Rao: Both supported. Node SDK is fine for your front-end proxy; Python has better sample notebooks for batching and evals. We'll include code snippets.
[24:16] Rachel Kim: About costs — can you provide an estimate of monthly spend for pilot?
[24:22] Avery Chen: We'll include a conservative run rate based on sample payloads, but rough ballpark in the quote. Expect cost to scale with token volume and model family; caching/batching can cut costs 30%+.
[24:38] Priya Sharma: Do you do penetration testing or can we run one?
[24:44] Avery Chen: We can share our SOC 2 scope. Customers can run scoped pen tests in Private deployments; we'll coordinate windows and required contacts.
[24:55] [crosstalk] Speaker 5: (overlapping)
[25:02] Avery Chen: Great, any other blockers?
[25:06] Lena Ortiz: None from my side.
[25:09] Marcus Doyle: No, timeline looks good.
[25:11] Priya Sharma: I'll review the security packet and follow up with any questions.
[25:15] Avery Chen: Thanks everyone. We'll follow up with the packet and the pilot quote.
[25:20] Maya Ortiz: I'll send calendar invites for weekly onboarding and the pilot kickoff.
[25:25] Rachel Kim: Thanks all.
[25:28] Avery Chen: Thanks, talk soon.

(End of recording — ~62 minutes total; transcript condensed to key timestamps and exchanges.)
